doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Electric bass and rock era
summary: He has played electric bass since 1958 for shows and as a hobby, and felt rock was simplistic though better today.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well the rock & roll scene came along, but I also owned an electric bass. I had gained one of those back in the Air Force days in the early 50s because Monk Montgomery used to play one, and one of the guys in the barracks was talking about he heard the bass and didn’t see a bass anywhere. And it turned out to be — this was with Lionel Hampton’s band.

The rock scene, everybody seemed to have been going toward that thing, that direction, so I pulled out my electric bass and played a few things, whatever they wanted me to play. It was like a cousin to me. It was like a hobby. I never took it seriously, although I’ve been playing electric bass since 1958. Like for shows, that type of thing, I always
pulled it out. Like the horse shows, the ice shows, that type of thing. Because you have to read. It’s like reading a book. You’ve done those shows, right?
